newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX starts firm, but all eyes on U.S..
newsitem.headline: German DAX starts firm, but all eyes on U.S..

text.p: A smattering of buy interest focused on export-driven chemical and car industries lifted German shares in early trade on Friday, but dealers were wary of labelling the move a clear change in trend.
The 30-share blue chip DAX index was up 23.17 points at 3,238.41 at 0851 GMT, holding firm despite a renewed overnight drop on Wall Street as fears of immminent rate increases continued.
"Monday is the earliest we will really be able to tell if we have found a real floor," said a Frankfurt dealer.
"There has been some real interest here, especially in chemicals, so it does look as though people are looking at fundamentals again. But we still have to wait for the U.S."

The advance included a surge of over four percent in shares of chemical firm BASF AG, which was up 2.60 marks at 64.10 marks after sending out a bullish outlook for 1997 this week and reporting well-received 1996 results.
Rival Hoechst was up 85 pfennigs at 64.45 marks.
The pace of decline on the German share market had already started to slow on Thursday, as prices started to approach interestingly low levels and more good corporate news emerged.

Nonetheless, attention was still focused on U.S. payroll data due at 1330 GMT, which is expected to give a strong clue on the outlook for the U.S. economy and provoke a firm reaction on the nervous U.S. stock market.
"I think we have already priced in bad news, but these things are very hard to call," another dealer said.
"I wouldn't rule out another tough Friday."
Car shares were also among big early gainers on Friday. Daimler Benz AG rose 1.45 marks to 123.15 marks and BMW was up nine marks at 1,228 marks.

Car and chemical shares had been expected to drive any recovery on the German share market as the mark remains broadly weak against most major currencies, improving the outlook considerably for export earnings.
